facts.statement: The genus Patagosuchus contains only one known species, Patagosuchus anielensis.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Patagosuchus anielensis.

facts.statement: Patagosuchus is distinguished by extremely heterodont dentition featuring small serrated front teeth and large, laterally compressed caniniform teeth behind them.
facts.quote: It is distinguished from other peirosaurids by its extremely heterodont dentition, which includes small serrated teeth at the front of the jaws with much larger, laterally compressed caniniform teeth behind them.

facts.statement: Patagosuchus possesses large interalveolar spaces between its teeth, a feature unique among peirosaurids.
facts.quote: Patagosuchus also has large spaces between its teeth called interalveolar spaces that are not found in any other peirosaurid.

facts.statement: Patagosuchus is known only from the holotype specimen MANE-PV 1, which represents a single individual.
facts.quote: Patagosuchus is known solely from its holotype, MANE-PV 1, which consists of some associated bones belonging to a single individual.

facts.statement: The holotype was discovered at the Baal Quarry in the Loma de La Lata area, 12 km south of Añelo City in Neuquén Province, Patagonia.
facts.quote: MANE-PV 1 was discovered at the Baal Quarry, in the Loma de La Lata area, near the northern coast of Lago Los Barreales, 12 km south of Añelo City, southeastern Neuquén Province of Patagonia.

facts.statement: Patagosuchus lived during the late Turonian to early Coniacian stages of the early Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Portezuelo Formation which is the older of the two formations in the Río Neuquén Subgroup, of the Neuquén Group, dating to the late Turonian to early Coniacian of the early Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Patagosuchus is the second peirosaurid described from the Portezuelo Formation, alongside Lomasuchus palpebrosus.
facts.quote: Patagosuchus is the second peirosaurid described from this formation, along with Lomasuchus palpebrosus.

facts.statement: Patagosuchus is the third peirosaurid named from the Neuquén Group, following Gasparinisuchus peirosauroides and preceding Bayomesasuchus hernandezi.
facts.quote: Patagosuchus represents the third peirosaurid named from the Neuquén Group, with Gasparinisuchus peirosauroides known from the younger Santonian to early Campanian Bajo de la Carpa and Anacleto Formations, and the more recently named Bayomesasuchus hernandezi from the underlying late Cenomanian to early Turonian Cerro Lisandro Formation representing the fourth.

facts.statement: Patagosuchus was first described and named by Lio, Agnolína, Juarez Valieri, Filippi, and Rosales in 2015.
facts.quote: Patagosuchus was first described and named by Gabrel Lio, Federico L. Agnolína, Rubén Juarez Valieri, Leonardo Filippi and Diego Rosales in 2015

facts.statement: The generic name Patagosuchus combines 'Patagonia' with 'suchus', derived from the Greek word for the Egyptian crocodile god.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to Patagonia, and suchus, Latinized from the Greek souchos, an Egyptian crocodile god.

facts.statement: The specific name anielensis refers to the city of Añelo near the discovery site.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to the city of Añelo, near which the holotype was discovered and collected.

facts.statement: The parent group of Patagosuchus is the family Peirosauridae.
Patagosuchus lived between 93.9 and 85.7 million years ago, during the Turonian to Coniacian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Coniacian (93.9 to 85.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Patagosuchus is an extinct genus of peirosaurid crocodyliform.
rejected.quote: Patagosuchus is an extinct genus of peirosaurid crocodyliform
